segments.he: הָתָם הָא אִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלְּקָחָן מִתְּחִלָּה לִבְהֵמָה, אֲבָל לְקָחָן מִתְּחִלָּה לְאָדָם וְנִמְלַךְ עֲלֵיהֶם לִבְהֵמָה – חַיָּיב לְעַשֵּׂר. וְהָתַנְיָא: הַלּוֹקֵחַ פֵּירוֹת מִן הַשּׁוּק לַאֲכִילָה וְנִמְלַךְ עֲלֵיהֶן לִבְהֵמָה – הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִתֵּן לֹא לִפְנֵי בְּהֶמְתּוֹ וְלֹא לִפְנֵי בֶּהֱמַת חֲבֵרוֹ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עִישֵּׂר.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «There, it was stated» with regard to that mishna that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: They taught» this «only» in a case «where one purchased» those items «initially for the animal» or for the other purposes enumerated in the mishna, «but» if «he purchased them initially for a person and reconsidered» his plans «for them» and decided to use them «for an animal, he is obligated to tithe» the demai. «And it is taught» in a baraita in support of that understanding: In the case of «one who purchases produce from the market for» human «consumption, and» he «reconsidered» his plans «for it» and decided to use it «for an animal, that» person «may neither place» it «before his animal nor before the animal of another unless he tithed» the produce.

segments.he: שְׁמַע רַבִּי, נְפַק לְאַפֵּיהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רְצוֹנְךָ סְעוֹד אֶצְלִי? אָמַר לוֹ: הֵן. צָהֲבוּ פָּנָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי.
segments.en: «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «heard» that Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir arrived, and he «emerged to greet him.» Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi «said to him:» Is it «your desire» to «dine with me?» Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir «said to him: Yes. Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi’s «face beamed [tzahavu],» as it was well known that Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir did not accept invitations to dine with others.

segments.he: אָמַר לוֹ: כִּמְדוּמֶּה אַתָּה שֶׁמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל אֲנִי? יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵן, יֵשׁ רוֹצֶה וְאֵין לוֹ, וְיֵשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ וְאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה, וּכְתִיב: ״אַל תִּלְחַם אֶת לֶחֶם רַע עָיִן וְאַל תִּתְאָיו לְמַטְעַמֹּתָיו כִּי כְּמוֹ שָׁעַר בְּנַפְשׁוֹ כֶּן הוּא אֱכוֹל וּשְׁתֵה יֹאמַר לָךְ וְלִבּוֹ בַּל עִמָּךְ״, וְאַתָּה רוֹצֶה וְיֵשׁ לְךָ.
segments.en: Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir «said to» Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi: «Are you under the impression that deriving benefit from the Jewish people is forbidden to me by vow?» On the contrary, «the Jewish people are holy.» I avoid accepting invitations, as «there is one who wants» to invite guests to dine with him «but he does not have» the means, and I do not want to enjoy a meal that my host cannot afford. «And there is one who has» the means «but does not want» to host guests, «and» with regard to those people «it is written: “Eat not the bread of him that has an evil eye, neither desire his delicacies. For as one that has reckoned within himself, so is he: Eat and drink, says he to you; but his heart is not with you”» (Proverbs 23:6–7). «But you want» to invite guests to dine with you, «and you have» the means.

segments.he: מִיהָא הַשְׁתָּא מְסַרְהֵיבְנָא, דִּבְמִלְּתָא דְּמִצְוָה קָא טָרַחְנָא, כִּי הָדַרְנָא אָתֵינָא עָיֵילְנָא לְגַבָּךְ.
segments.en: «But now I am rushing [mesarheivna], as I am engaged in» the performance of «a matter involving a mitzva. When I come back I will enter to» dine with «you.»

segments.he: כִּי אֲתָא, אִיתְרְמִי עָל בְּהָהוּא פִּיתְחָא דַּהֲווֹ קָיְימִין בֵּיהּ כּוּדַנְיָיתָא חִוָּורָתָא, אָמַר: מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת בְּבֵיתוֹ שֶׁל זֶה וַאֲנִי אֶסְעוֹד אֶצְלוֹ?
segments.en: «When» Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir «came» back, «he happened to enter through that entrance in which white mules were standing. He said: The Angel of Death» is «in this» person’s «house, and I will eat with him?» White mules were known to be dangerous animals.

segments.he: שְׁמַע רַבִּי נְפַק לְאַפֵּיהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מְזַבֵּנְינָא לְהוּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״וְלִפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל״.
segments.en: «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «heard» the comment of Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir and «emerged to greet him. He said to him: I will sell» the mules. Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir «said to him:» You will thereby violate the prohibition: «“Nor place a stumbling block before the blind”» (Leviticus 19:14), as it is prohibited for any Jew to keep a destructive animal in his possession.

segments.he: מַפְקַרְנָא לְהוּ, מַפְּשַׁתְּ הֶיזֵּקָא. עָקַרְנָא לְהוּ, אִיכָּא צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים. קָטֵילְנָא לְהוּ, אִיכָּא ״בַּל תַּשְׁחִית״.
segments.en: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said to him: «I will declare» the mules «ownerless.» Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir said to him: «You» will thereby «increase the damage,» as there will be no owner to restrain it. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said to him: «I» will «remove their» hooves so that they will be unable to kick and cause damage. Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir said to him: «There is» the requirement to prevent «suffering to animals,» and you will be violating it. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said to him: «I» will «kill them.» Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir said to him: «There is» the prohibition: «Do not destroy» items of value.

segments.he: הֲוָה קָא מְבַתֵּשׁ בֵּיהּ טוּבָא, גְּבַהּ טוּרָא בֵּינַיְיהוּ, בָּכָה רַבִּי וְאָמַר: מָה בְּחַיֵּיהֶן כָּךְ, בְּמִיתָתָן עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה! דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: גְּדוֹלִים צַדִּיקִים בְּמִיתָתָן יוֹתֵר מִבְּחַיֵּיהֶן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי הֵם קוֹבְרִים אִישׁ וְהִנֵּה רָאוּ הַגְּדוּד וַיַּשְׁלִיכוּ אֶת הָאִישׁ בְּקֶבֶר אֱלִישָׁע וַיֵּלֶךְ וַיִּגַּע הָאִישׁ בְּעַצְמוֹת אֱלִישָׁע וַיְחִי וַיָּקׇם עַל רַגְלָיו״.
segments.en: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi «was greatly imploring him» to enter his home until «a mountain rose between them» and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi could no longer speak with him. «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «wept and said: If during their lifetimes» it is «so» that the righteous are great, «after their death» it is «all the more so» true. The Gemara comments: This is «as Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina says: The righteous are greater after their death, more so than during their lifetimes, as it is stated: “And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that they spied a raiding party; and they cast the man into the tomb of Elisha; and as soon as the man touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet”» (II Kings 13:21).

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְדִילְמָא לְקַיּוֹמֵי בֵּיהּ בִּרְכְּתָא דְּאֵלִיָּהוּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וִיהִי נָא פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּרוּחֲךָ אֵלָי״? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דְּתַנְיָא: עַל רַגְלָיו עָמַד, וּלְבֵיתוֹ לֹא הָלַךְ!
segments.en: «Rav Pappa said to Abaye:» This proof from the case of Elisha that the righteous are greater after death is not valid. «And perhaps» this transpired «to fulfill with regard to» Elisha «the blessing of Elijah, as it is written: “Please, let a double portion of your spirit be upon me”» (II Kings 2:9). Elijah revived one dead person and this one is the second revived by Elisha. Abaye «said to» Rav Pappa: «If so, is this» consistent with that «which is taught» in a baraita: The dead person «arose on his feet but he did not go to his home,» indicating that he had not truly been revived?

segments.he: אֶלָּא בְּמָה אִיקַּיַּים? כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁרִיפֵּא צָרַעַת נַעֲמָן, שֶׁהִיא שְׁקוּלָה כְּמֵת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַל נָא תְהִי כַּמֵּת״.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But» if that is the case, «in what» manner «was» Elijah’s blessing «fulfilled?» It is «as Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» The blessing was fulfilled «when he cured the leprosy of Naaman, since» a leper «is equivalent to a dead person, as it is stated» with regard to Miriam when she was afflicted with leprosy: «“Please, let her not be as one dead”» (Numbers 12:12).

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָן ״יֵמִים״ – שֶׁאֵימָתָם מוּטֶּלֶת עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מִיָּמַי לֹא שְׁאָלַנִי אָדָם עַל מַכַּת פִּרְדָּה לְבָנָה וְחָיָה. וְהָא קָחָזֵינָא דְּחָיֵי! אֵימָא: ״וְחָיָית״, וְהָא קָחָזֵינָא דְּמִיתַּסֵּי! דְּחִיוָּורָן רֵישׁ כַּרְעַיְיהוּ קָא אָמְרִינַן.
segments.en: Apropos white mules, which were likened to the Angel of Death, «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: Why are» the mules «called yemim» (see Genesis 36:24)? It is «because their terror [eimatam] is cast over» all «creatures, as Rabbi Ḥanina says: In» all «my days, no man has asked me about a wound» caused him «by a white mule and survived,» indicating that they are extremely dangerous. The Gemara asks: «But haven’t we seen that» some people «survive» after being wounded by a white mule? The Gemara answers: «Say» instead, no man has asked me about a wound caused him by a mule «and» the wound «healed.» The Gemara asks: «But haven’t we seen that» such wounds «heal?» The Gemara answers: The wound that «we say» does not heal is one caused by a mule «the top of whose legs are white.»

segments.he: ״אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ״ – אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: וַאֲפִילּוּ כְּשָׁפִים. הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּהֲוָת קָא מְהַדְּרָא לְמִישְׁקַל עַפְרָא מִתּוּתֵי כַּרְעֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, אֲמַר לַהּ: שְׁקוּלִי, לָא מִסְתַּיְּיעָא מִילְּתִיךְ, ״אֵין עוֹד מִלְבַדּוֹ״ כְּתִיב. וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָן כְּשָׁפִים – שֶׁמַּכְחִישִׁין פָּמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה! שָׁאנֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא דִּנְפִישָׁא זְכוּתֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara relates other statements of Rabbi Ḥanina: With regard to the verse: «“There is none else beside Him”» (Deuteronomy 4:35), «Rabbi Ḥanina says: And even sorcery» is ineffective against the will of God. The Gemara relates: There was «a certain woman who would try to take dust from beneath the feet of Rabbi Ḥanina» in order to perform sorcery on him and harm him. Rabbi Ḥanina «said to her: Take» the dust, but «the matter will be ineffective for you,» as it «is written: “There is none other beside Him.”» The Gemara asks: «But doesn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say: Why» is sorcery «called keshafim?» It is an acronym for «makhḥishin pamalya shel mala,» meaning: «That they diminish the heavenly entourage [pamalya],» indicating that they function contrary to the will of God. The Gemara answers: «Rabbi Ḥanina is different, as,» because «his merit is great,» sorcery has no effect on him.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אֵין אָדָם נוֹקֵף אֶצְבָּעוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מַכְרִיזִין עָלָיו מִלְּמַעְלָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מֵה׳ מִצְעֲדֵי גֶבֶר כּוֹנָנוּ וְאָדָם מַה יָּבִין דַּרְכּוֹ״. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: דַּם נִיקּוּף מְרַצֶּה כְּדַם עוֹלָה. אָמַר רָבָא: בְּגוּדָל יָמִין, וּבְנִיקּוּף שֵׁנִי, וְהוּא דְּקָאָזֵיל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Ḥanina says: A person injures his finger below,» on earth, «only if they declare about him on high» that he should be injured, «as it is stated: It is of the Lord that a man’s goings are established; and a man, what does he understand of his way» (see Psalms 37:23 and Proverbs 20:24). «Rabbi Elazar says: The blood of a wound effects atonement like the blood of a burnt offering. Rava said:» This is stated «with regard to» a wound on his «right thumb,» as one applies force with that thumb and the wound is consequently more severe; «and» it is also stated «with regard to a second wound» in the same place before the first has healed, «and it is» provided «that» he is wounded while «going to» perform «a matter» involving «a mitzva.»

segments.he: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר: מִיָּמָיו לֹא בָּצַע עַל פְּרוּסָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁלּוֹ, וּמִיּוֹם שֶׁעָמַד עַל דַּעְתּוֹ לֹא נֶהֱנָה מִסְּעוּדַת אָבִיו.
segments.en: Apropos Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir, the Gemara notes that «they said about Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir: In» all «his days he never broke» bread and recited a blessing «on a piece of bread that was not his, and from the day that he achieved cognition he did not benefit» even «from the meal of his father,» because he eschewed benefit from everyone.

moves.summary: A baraita is cited on the Abaye-Rava dispute of the previous unit: a Samaritan's slaughter is permitted when a Jew stands over him; otherwise he is tested by being fed an olive-bulk.
moves.about: brings the baraita on a Samaritan's slaughter to bear on the Abaye-Rava dispute over the mishna

moves.summary: The baraita's parallel clause: a string of birds found with a Samaritan is tested by giving him one bird's head to eat.
Abaye reads the first clause: only actual supervision permits, so exiting and entering does not.
moves.about: whether a Jew who exits and enters counts as standing over the Samaritan

moves.summary: Rava reads the latter clause: the test is needed only where the Jew was absent, so exiting and entering permits.
moves.about: whether a Jew who exits and enters counts as adequate supervision

moves.summary: The latter clause is pressed against Abaye.
moves.about: the latter clause of the baraita, which requires a test when the Jew was absent, is hard for Abaye

moves.cueHe: אמר לך: יוצא ונכנס נמי ״בא ומצאו״ קרי ליה
moves.summary: A defence is supplied for Abaye: the tanna calls exiting-and-entering itself 'came and found him'.
moves.about: Abaye could reply that the tanna calls exiting-and-entering itself 'came and found him'

moves.summary: The first clause is pressed against Rava.
moves.about: the first clause of the baraita, which requires the Jew to stand over him, is hard for Rava

moves.cueHe: אמר לך: יוצא ונכנס נמי כעומד על גביו דמי
moves.summary: A defence is supplied for Rava: exiting-and-entering counts as standing over him.
moves.about: Rava could reply that exiting-and-entering is reckoned as standing over him

moves.summary: Why is the bird test reliable — perhaps only the bird whose head he was given was slaughtered properly.
moves.about: why feeding the Samaritan one bird's head proves the rest were properly slaughtered

moves.summary: Rav Menashe: the Jew hides the birds under his garment so the Samaritan cannot tell which head he ate.
moves.about: the case is one where the Jew hides the birds under his garment so the Samaritan cannot tell which head he was given

moves.summary: A mnemonic for the three statements of Rav Menashe in this tractate.
moves.about: a memory-sign fixing the three statements of Rav Menashe in this tractate

moves.cueHe: ודלמא סימנא הוה יהיב ליה בגויה
moves.summary: Perhaps the Samaritan marked the one bird he slaughtered properly.
moves.about: perhaps the Samaritan had placed a distinguishing mark in the one bird he did slaughter properly

moves.summary: Rav Mesharshiyya: the head is crushed, so no mark can be recognised.
moves.about: the Jew crushes the head he gives him, so no mark can be recognised

moves.summary: Perhaps Samaritans hold that bird slaughter is not required by the Torah, so his eating proves nothing.
moves.about: perhaps Samaritans hold there is no Torah requirement to slaughter a bird, so his eating proves nothing

moves.summary: On that reasoning the disqualifications of slaughter are equally unwritten, yet Samaritans are relied on for them.
moves.about: on its own concern, the disqualifications of slaughter are equally unwritten, yet Samaritans are relied on for them

moves.summary: Once the Samaritans embraced a practice they keep it as Jews do — bird slaughter included.
moves.about: once the Samaritans embraced a practice they keep it as Jews do, so bird slaughter too

moves.cueHe: ואחזוק ולא אחזוק בדלא כתיבא, תנאי היא, דתניא
moves.summary: That principle is itself a tannaitic dispute: a baraita permits Samaritan matza on Passover.
moves.about: shows that whether Samaritans are presumed to keep unwritten mitzvot is itself a tannaitic dispute

moves.summary: R' Elazar forbids it, because Samaritans are not expert in the details of mitzvot.
moves.about: whether a Samaritan's matza may be eaten on Passover and used to fulfil the obligation

moves.summary: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: whatever mitzva Samaritans embraced they keep more exactingly than Jews.
moves.about: on what basis Samaritans may be relied on for a mitzva — that it is written in the Torah, or that they embraced it

moves.summary: The baraita's first clause is re-cited for analysis.
moves.about: re-cites the baraita's opening clause for analysis

moves.summary: If the matza is permitted, that one fulfils the obligation with it is self-evident.
moves.about: that once the matza is permitted, fulfilling the obligation with it is self-evident and need not be taught

moves.summary: A candidate misconstrual is floated: that Samaritans are not expert in guarding the matza.
moves.about: that R' Elazar's prohibition rests on Samaritans not being expert in guarding the matza

moves.summary: The tanna teaches us that they are expert — that is the novelty.
moves.about: the novelty is that Samaritans are expert in guarding the matza for the sake of the mitzva

moves.summary: R' Elazar's prohibition is grounded: he holds Samaritans are not expert in guarding.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel appears to say exactly what the first tanna said.
moves.about: that his statement adds nothing to the first tanna's

moves.cueHe: איכא בינייהו דכתיבא ולא אחזיקו בה
moves.summary: They differ over a written mitzva the Samaritans are not known to have embraced.
moves.about: they differ over a mitzva written in the Torah that the Samaritans are not known to have embraced

moves.summary: On that reading his wording should have been 'if they embraced', not 'any mitzva that they embraced'.
moves.about: that on this reading Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel should have said 'if they embraced', not 'any mitzva that they embraced'

moves.cueHe: אלא, איכא בינייהו דלא כתיבא ואחזיקו בה
moves.summary: They differ instead over an unwritten mitzva the Samaritans did embrace.
moves.about: they differ instead over a mitzva not written in the Torah that the Samaritans did embrace

moves.summary: Rava's earlier ruling is taken up in its own right: for a transgressor who eats carcasses out of appetite, one examines a knife and gives it to him.
moves.about: returns to Rava's ruling on a transgressor who eats carcasses out of appetite, to treat it in its own right

moves.summary: Why may such a transgressor be relied on?
moves.about: why a transgressor given an examined knife may be relied on

moves.summary: One who transgresses out of appetite will not choose the forbidden when the permitted is equally to hand.
moves.about: one who transgresses out of appetite will not choose the forbidden when the permitted is equally available

moves.cueHe: אי הכי, כי לא בדק נמי
moves.summary: Then examining the knife should be unnecessary altogether.
moves.about: if that reasoning holds, examining the knife should be unnecessary altogether

moves.summary: He will not trouble himself to replace a flawed knife, so the examination is still needed.
moves.about: a transgressor will not trouble himself to replace a flawed knife, so the examination is still needed

moves.cueHe: אמרו ליה רבנן לרבא: תניא דמסייע לך
moves.summary: The Sages bring Rava a supporting baraita: transgressors' leaven is permitted after Passover because they exchange it.
moves.about: brings the baraita on transgressors' leavened bread after Passover before Rava

moves.cueHe: סברוה, הא מני? רבי יהודה היא
moves.summary: The proof was assumed to follow R' Yehuda, for whom leaven after Passover is forbidden by Torah law.
moves.about: R' Yehuda's ruling that leaven after Passover is forbidden by Torah law

moves.summary: Perhaps it follows R' Shimon, so the leniency is only rabbinic and proves nothing.
moves.about: perhaps the baraita follows R' Shimon, for whom the leniency is only rabbinic and proves nothing for a Torah prohibition

moves.summary: Even on R' Shimon's view the baraita states the exchange as fact, and an a fortiori carries it to Torah prohibitions.
moves.about: even on R' Shimon's view the baraita states exchange as fact, and the a fortiori holds

moves.summary: The הכל שוחטין baraita is floated as support for Rava.
moves.about: brings the הכל שוחטין baraita as candidate support for Rava

moves.summary: What kind of uncircumcised man does the baraita mean?
moves.about: that the uncircumcised man of the baraita cannot be one whose brothers died of circumcision, for he is a full-fledged Jew

moves.summary: A candidate: one whose brothers died of circumcision.
moves.about: whether the baraita's 'even a Jewish transgressor' is the very case Rava permitted

moves.summary: That candidate falls: such a man is a full-fledged Jew, not a transgressor.
He must be one who refuses circumcision, so a transgressor in one matter is not a transgressor in all.
The latter clause must therefore mean a transgressor in the very matter of slaughter — as Rava held.
moves.about: that the latter clause must mean a transgressor in the very matter of slaughter, as Rava held

moves.summary: The support fails: one accustomed to the transgression treats it as permitted.
moves.about: the support fails: a transgressor in the very matter is accustomed to it and treats it as permitted

moves.cueHe: אלא משומד לעבודה זרה, וכדרב ענן
moves.summary: The baraita instead speaks of a transgressor with regard to idolatry, following Rav Anan.
